authors: Alnaqbi, A.; Zeiada, W.; Al-Khateeb, G. G.
title: A hybrid machine learning method of support vector regression with particle swarm optimization for predicting IRI in continuously reinforced concrete pavement
role_in_review: PRIMARY — §7 & §10 FULL-TEXT-VERIFIED leakage case & same-substrate series (1 of 14+)
note: FULL-TEXT VERIFIED (not abstract-level): fetched full text confirms the 5-fold split is described as 'The dataset was split into 5 subsets, and the model was trained and tested 5 times, each time using a different subset as the test set and the remaining subsets as the training set' -- a plain random split at OBSERVATION level with NO mention of section-level grouping across the paper's full methodology section. Predictor normalization (z-score) is described in 'Data preparation techniques', textually preceding the cross-validation description, consistent with (though not proof of) normalization computed on the full dataset before the split. The paper's own Limitations section states: 'Only fivefold cross-validation was used ... no independent testing was done using additional datasets' -- a self-declared absence of external validation. The authors defend against an overfitting concern by noting RMSE is stable across folds (0.02791-0.06422) -- but stable RMSE across folds is exactly what unaddressed section-level leakage would ALSO produce, since every fold would share the same leakage pathway; fold-to-fold consistency is evidence against fold-selection luck, not evidence against leakage. leakage_risk: HIGH (confirmed, not inferred). external_validation: NO (author-confirmed). This paper is the review's worked example of full-text-confirmed coding and should anchor the worked-example paragraph in the PAVE-ML instrument (Section 10).

authors: Huang, H.; Xu, Z.; Li, X.; et al.
title: Predicting rheological properties of asphalt modified with mineral powder: bagging, boosting, and stacking vs. single machine learning models
role_in_review: PRIMARY — §9, §10 FULL-TEXT-VERIFIED positive exemplar (leakage-avoidance design confirmed)
note: FULL-TEXT VERIFIED (fourth confirmed case, and the first POSITIVE exemplar confirmed rather than a risk): Section 3.3 states explicitly 'the training set, fitted by base learners as input for the meta-learner, can cause information leakage and overfitting. Thus, this study improves traditional ensemble algorithms by using cross-validation (CV) in the first-level base learner construction' -- followed by a precise formal description (S1...Sk training folds, Sk+1 test fold, Tr/Te predictions) that matches a textbook leakage-safe stacking implementation. Section 3.5 separately confirms hyperparameter optimisation was 'restricted to the meta-learner to mitigate overfitting' and that final accuracy was assessed on a genuinely held-out portion. This is a design that does what its abstract claims, verified rather than taken on faith -- the correct complement to the three risk-confirmations elsewhere in this database, and the reason this paper anchors the positive PAVE-ML worked example (Section 10) rather than being asserted as positive from the abstract alone. One caveat for consistency: external_validation still codes NO under the strict §2.3 criterion -- all data come from the authors' own DSR tests (2 emulsifiers x 3 mineral powders), not an independently sourced dataset -- so this paper is a genuine positive case for leakage avoidance specifically, not a paper that clears every PAVE-ML criterion.

authors: Xiao, W.; Wang, C.; Liu, J.; Gao, M.; Wu, J.
title: Optimizing faulting prediction for rigid pavements using a hybrid SHAP-TPE-CatBoost model
role_in_review: PRIMARY — §7 & §10 FULL-TEXT-VERIFIED leakage case (3rd confirmed, distinct mechanism)
note: FULL-TEXT VERIFIED (third confirmed leakage case, different mechanism from the CRCP series): the paper's own section structure resolves the ambiguity definitively. Section 3.2 'Boruta-Based Feature Selection' is performed as part of Section 3 'Data Preparation', over the full 160-observation dataset, BEFORE Section 4 'Model Construction' states 'As shown in Figure 3, 80% of the processed data were used as the training set... the remaining 20% were used as the test set.' Boruta therefore selected features using information from what later became the test set -- a textbook feature-selection leak, confirmed by the paper's own section ordering rather than inferred. The paper's own conclusion attributes part of its headline result to this step: 'Compared to the TPE-CatBoost model constructed with 17 variables, there was an increase of 0.007 in R2... attributed to the capability of Boruta to identify relevant variables' -- meaning the improvement the paper highlights is exactly the part most exposed to the leak. Separately, K-fold CV is used correctly, but only for hyperparameter tuning inside the 80% training portion -- a genuine held-out 20% test set does exist, which makes this leakage pathway narrower than the CRCP series (a real test set, contaminated only by pre-split feature selection, rather than no grouping at all). leakage_risk: HIGH (confirmed, pre-split feature selection). external_validation: not explicitly no, but the conclusion calls the method only 'preliminarily validated' and calls for an expanded dataset in future work. This is the review's third full-text-confirmed case and the first from a different research team, and it demonstrates leakage in this literature is not one single failure mode but at least two distinct ones: ungrouped cross-validation (Alnaqbi series, §7) and pre-split feature selection (this paper) -- both caught by the same PAVE-ML leakage-risk item, for different underlying reasons.

note: SAME-SUBSTRATE SERIES: one of at least 14 identified single-target papers by an overlapping author team (Alnaqbi, Zeiada, Al-Khateeb, and variously Abuzwidah/Hamad/Barakat/Nasr), all drawing on the same ~33-section, ~385-395-observation CRCP LTPP substrate, each pairing a different metaheuristic (mostly PSO or GA) with a different base learner (mostly SVR or GBM) to predict a different single target (IRI, longitudinal cracking, transverse cracking, spalling, punchouts, faulting, friction number, rutting), each via five-fold CV, each reporting R2 in the 0.90-0.99 range. authors: Alnaqbi, A.; Al-Khateeb, G.; Zeiada, W.
title: Predictive modeling of longitudinal cracking in CRCP using PSO-tuned gradient boosting machines
role_in_review: PRIMARY — §7 & §10 FULL-TEXT-VERIFIED leakage case (2nd confirmed) & same-substrate series (2 of 14+)
note: FULL-TEXT VERIFIED (second confirmed case in the series, replicating 10.1186/s44147-025-00706-9): methods state plainly 'Five equal-sized subsets were randomly selected from the dataset... the training and testing subsets were switched around in each iteration' -- again a random split at OBSERVATION level with no section-level grouping across the paper's methods section. z-score normalization, missing-value imputation, and IQR-based outlier removal are all described within a single 'data preprocessing stage' that textually precedes the cross-validation description, with no statement that any of these steps were refit per fold. The paper's own Future Directions section separately lists 'External dataset validation' as unmet future work -- a second self-admission of no external validation, independent of the first paper's. leakage_risk: HIGH (confirmed). external_validation: NO (author-confirmed, second instance). This paper ALSO reproduces, in its own Table 1, a literature summary of other rigid-pavement LTPP ML studies that substantially overlaps with the same-substrate series documented in this review's Section 7 -- the authors are aware of the surrounding literature's density on this exact substrate, which sharpens rather than excuses the absence of any discussion of shared-substrate or shared-personnel effects across their own papers.
